_comment: The countries VisaAI is in scope for. Single source of truth — the generators
read this file, so the coverage matrix, the exception ledger and the §84
baseline all measure against the same list.
SET BY SCOPE DECISIONS, not by attrition. The specification originally
mandated a 195-country floor (193 UN member states plus the Holy See and the
State of Palestine). It was replaced on 2026-08-24; §4.1 records the change.
Revised the same day to 37: the five countries already probed (Austria,
Denmark, France, Japan, Portugal) were kept IN scope rather than stranded,
and China was added. Their probe evidence in country-probe-evidence.json
therefore counts toward the §84 row again rather than being filed as history.
Countries outside this list REMAIN in visa_countries. They are not deleted:
they carry support_state='unsupported', publish nothing, and can be brought
back into scope by editing this file. Deleting them would make the decision
irreversible and would lie about what the registry knows.
'Middle East' has no agreed membership. The broad geopolitical reading was
chosen — the Gulf states, the Levant, Iran, Iraq, Israel, plus Turkey, Egypt
and Cyprus. Written down here because the next person will otherwise have to
guess which of the several possible lists was meant.
